title: Per-port floor of fifteen rank-one requests for the thin query stages (atlas P8 impossible per port; no new kappa)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Matarener"} -->
_Requested by **Mark** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01S3pGeUvPqSHrKehUdW1spL?thread=cmsg_01S3pGeUvPqSHrKehUdW1spLQhAukggq3q4QdPKpxs2TAW)_

**Scoped negative result; no new κ.** Package `research/p104-thin-query-port-floor`, base `19fdb086e`.

Atlas target **P8** (PR5586, `provider-targets.md`) asks for a causal linear realization of the 15 chronological `QUERY_SHEAR` stages of the direct controller with at most 528 rank-one requests in total (in place of 15 × ports), each latent channel evaluated on a currently available linear combination of fields, the 18 full calls kept. This package shows that on every central port the 15 shear results are **linearly independent modulo everything that is free** (scalar ADD, swaps, even central powers, markers, plus the 18 paid full-call outputs): the free span has dimension 49, the free span plus the 15 results has dimension 64 (the whole port space). So any realization in that model needs **at least 15 requests per port**, i.e. at least the present count: 1,680 on the PR5398 direct controller, 1,560 on the p104 productive word. The same holds on the joint-helper-lattice source controller. Each result is also independent of the free span plus the other 14 (order of events irrelevant), and the greedy causal realization attains 15, so P8's "two consecutive stages in fewer requests" is negative as well.

Argument: a rank-one channel on one available content `v` yields an element of `R·v` with `R = K[Q, Q⁻¹]`, and `Q^{2k}v` is free, so each channel adds at most one generator to the free span; after `m` channels every content lies in `F + span(q_1..q_m)`, and the 15 results must lie there. Stage markers are specialised to 1 and `Q²` to a scalar (7/3 and 11/5); both are ring homomorphisms, so the specialised count is a valid lower bound.

Together with `research/thin-query-shear-floor` (#4603: fusion with a full call needs two queries; parity floor 15) the per-port answer for the thin stages is complete. The only route left for P8 is a channel that serves several port lines at once, which is a new physical primitive outside the present price list (the P104 contract fixes a central port and a 17-axis route per port); it is listed as the open question, not excluded.

**Verification** (under a second, standard library):

```sh
python3.12 -B research/p104-thin-query-port-floor/verify.py
```

Pinned inputs (the three controllers, `caller.py`, the atlas targets); exact rational ranks on all three controllers for both central squares; every result against the other 14; greedy count; controls: a redundant sixteenth shear (the output of the last full call on its own pair) is recognised as free with the floor unchanged, the flawed model that treats present contents as free collapses to 0, and declaring odd central powers free collapses to 0; RESULT.json compared in full. `scripts/research_package.py` passes (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, outcome=completed).

Per-port, linear, scalar model only; native maps, caller, compiler and outer checks are not involved. Selected record unchanged. Agent check, not human acceptance. Credit: Cinna Davis (controllers), Ali Romman (PR5398), Dugongue (atlas PR5586) and the P104 lineage; nothing of theirs is modified. Prepared by Matarener with Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code.
